events.desc: Penelope Pitstop: Well, I do declare! What a magnificent old manor! Just look at that chandelier — oh my stars, it's practically dripping with history and dust in equal measure! I am just tickled pink to be here with all y'all fine people. Now then, I have a feeling this grand old place is just bursting at the seams with secrets, and I intend to find every last one of them — starting with that legendary Doily Diamond! But a proper Southern lady always takes in the lay of the land before chargin' off on an adventure. Let me get a good look at this foyer!

Oh, this is going to be simply wonderful! All these characters gathered together in one place — why, it's like a party just waiting to happen! And somewhere in this dusty old mansion, the Doily Diamond is waiting for someone clever enough to find it. That someone is going to be me, Clara Bellingham! Now, that guest book might tell me who else has been poking around this place, and the library — oh, libraries always have the best clues. I just know it!

The Hooded Claw (as Sneekly): Welcome, welcome, most esteemed guests, to Doily Manor! I am Pemberton, humble estate manager and your devoted servant for this evening's... festivities. If you'll permit me, I shall just consult the guest book to ensure all our expected visitors have arrived safely. One does so worry about stragglers on these dark country roads...

Pemberton, the doddering fool — how deliciously easy to wear this mask! But where is Clara Bellingham? She is NOT among these guests. Every moment she wanders unsupervised is a moment she might stumble upon the treasure that is RIGHTFULLY mine. I must find her — but first, the guest book. Knowledge is the foundation upon which all truly magnificent schemes are built!

The Ant Hill Mob: Alright lads, listen up! We've arrived at Doily Manor and Clara ain't here in this room — which means she could be ANYWHERE in this spooky old gaff, possibly in MORTAL DANGER! Now, nobody panic — The Brixton Boys have got this under control. First things first, we case this entrance hall top to bottom. That chandelier up there? Looks like it could drop any second. And that guest book — could have CLUES about who's been here before us. Everyone stay sharp, stay together, and remember — we're here for Clara!

I don't like the look of that Sneekly fella. There's something off about him — the way he lurks about, too quiet, too... helpful-looking. But I'm not one to point fingers. Still, the lads and me, we'll be keeping one eye on him, mark my words. And that chandelier really does look like a death trap waiting to happen.

Dick Dastardly: Ah, what a MAGNIFICENT estate! I, Reginald Foxworth — decorated explorer and three-time recipient of the Royal Geographical Society's Medal of Distinction — have graced these halls with my presence. You may all relax now. The treasure, whatever it may be, is practically found already. But first — one must always sign the guest book. It's only civilised.

None of those medals exist, naturally. But confidence is ninety percent of the con, and I am ONE HUNDRED percent confident. Now let's see what secrets this guest book holds — previous visitors always leave trails, and trails lead to TREASURE.

Peter Perfect: James Hartwell strides into Doily Manor and finds it... magnificent! Dusty, yes — perilous chandelier, certainly — but magnificent nonetheless! Good evening, ladies and gentlemen! I am James Hartwell, and I have come on a matter of the utmost importance. But first — a gentleman always signs the guest book. It is the done thing, and James Hartwell always does the done thing!

Clara is not here. My heart sinks — but only momentarily! She must be elsewhere in the manor. I shall sign this guest book, gather intelligence from these colourful characters, and then find her. A plan is forming... an elaborate plan, naturally. Step one: the guest book. Step two: inquire about Clara's whereabouts. Step three: proceed to her location with maximum gallantry. Step four through seventeen can be determined en route.

Penelope Pitstop: Oh my stars, where are my manners? Everyone and their cousin has already had a peek at this guest book and here I am just gawkin' at the chandelier like a tourist! Pemberton, sugar, you are just the most attentive host — why, I feel right at home already! Now let me have a look-see at this guest book. A lady always signs in, and besides — you never know what little secrets a guest book might be holdin' onto!

Everyone's crowded around that guest book like bees to honey — there must be somethin' worth seein' in there! And after that, I have got to get myself into that library. Floor-to-ceiling bookshelves and a carved stone mantelpiece with an inscription? Why, that inscription alone could be the key to finding the Doily Diamond! But first things first, Clara — guest book, then library. One step at a time... even if my heart is racin' with excitement!

The Hooded Claw (as Sneekly): Most gracious of you all to sign in so promptly — it warms this old servant's heart, it truly does! I see from the register that all our expected guests have indeed arrived, including the estimable Miss Bellingham, though she appears to have... wandered ahead. Most enterprising of her! Now, if you'll permit me, I must attend to a few matters about the manor — ensuring the rooms are properly aired, the candles lit, that sort of tedious domestic business. One does want everything to be JUST so for such distinguished visitors. Please, do make yourselves entirely at home. The manor is yours to explore!

Clara Bellingham is in this manor — the guest book CONFIRMS it — but she has already slipped away from the group! Every second she spends alone is a second she might find the treasure before I can stop her. The library — oh, it MUST be the library! That inscription on the mantelpiece practically SCREAMS 'clue.' I shall glide there under the pretence of lighting candles and airing rooms. And when I find dear Clara... well. That precariously hanging chandelier gave me such WONDERFUL ideas. But first — locate the prey. The hunt begins NOW!

The Ant Hill Mob: Oi oi oi! Listen up, everyone — we've checked this guest book and Clara Bellingham ain't signed it! That means she's either not here yet or she's already wandered off into this death trap of a manor on her own! Now, the Brixton Boys don't leave a lady unprotected — that's Rule Number One in the Brixton Boys' Code of Honour, page four, paragraph six, subsection B! We're heading to the Library to conduct a THOROUGH and PROFESSIONAL search! Lads — Formation Delta! Single file! And nobody — I repeat NOBODY — touch that chandelier on the way past!

The lads are terrified but they won't show it — bless 'em. Clive's already tripped over his own shoelaces twice and we haven't even left the entrance hall. But we WILL find Clara, even if we have to turn this whole manor upside down. That Sneekly — sorry, 'Pemberton' — he was awfully keen on that guest book. Checking for stragglers, he said. Or checking who's here so he knows who to pick off? No no, that's not fair. Give the man a chance. But I'm watching him. The Brixton Boys are ALWAYS watching.

Dick Dastardly: Ladies and gentlemen — and Muttley — I have made a MOST extraordinary discovery! The guest book contains a notation from the late Lord Doily himself, dated 1887. It reads — and I quote, for I have a photographic memory, naturally — 'The treasure sleeps where the copper sings at midnight.' COPPER, you see! Copper pots! The KITCHEN! The treasure is almost certainly concealed beneath the kitchen floor or within the old wood-burning stove. I suggest — nay, I IMPLORE you all — to make haste to the kitchen immediately. Every moment wasted here is a moment the treasure remains unfound! Go, go, GO! I shall follow shortly — I simply must make one final note in the guest book. A man of my stature always leaves his mark.

Ha HA! 'The copper sings at midnight' — I just invented that on the spot! Pure GENIUS! There is no such notation in that guest book. But they don't know that, do they? While these credulous simpletons go banging about the kitchen looking for singing copper pots, I shall waltz into the library and examine that carved stone mantelpiece inscription. THAT is where the real clue lies — any fool can see it. Well, any fool who is also a genius. Which is just ME. Oh, Reginald, you magnificent, scheming devil — the Doily Diamond is practically in your pocket already!
Peter Perfect spoke quietly with hooded-claw.

My heart is positively thundering! Clara must be somewhere deeper in the manor. The Library, perhaps — a woman of her intellect would naturally be drawn to books. Or the Kitchen — though that seems less romantic. I shall try the Library first. A gentleman always assumes the best of a lady's pursuits. And if she is not there, James Hartwell shall search every room, every corridor, every dusty corner of this magnificent old pile until he finds her!

Penelope Pitstop: Well now, that guest book was just full of interesting tidbits! Dick Dastardly, sugar, that was a mighty fine observation about the copper — but you know what they say back home: 'Don't chase the first fox out of the brush!' That library has a carved stone mantelpiece with an inscription on it, and in my experience, when a manor house goes to the trouble of carving words into STONE, those words mean somethin'! Professor Pat Pending, Sergeant Blast, y'all are welcome to join me — the more the merrier, I always say! Now if you'll excuse me, I am headin' to that library before all the good clues are spoken for!

Dick Dastardly sendin' everyone to the kitchen while he supposedly stays behind to 'sign the guest book'? And then he went to the library anyway? That man is up to somethin', but I just can't bring myself to think ill of him — maybe he changed his mind! And Pemberton vanishin' into the library the moment the pleasantries were done... well, an estate manager has business everywhere in a house, doesn't he? Focus, Clara — that mantelpiece inscription is the real prize. A diamond as famous as the Doily Diamond wouldn't be hidden behind somethin' as obvious as a copper pot clue. It'd be hidden behind poetry and riddles and carved stone. That's where MY talents shine!

The Hooded Claw (as Sneekly): Ah, welcome to the library, distinguished guests! Do forgive the dust — the manor has been without proper staff for some years, I'm afraid. Now, if you'll permit me just a moment, I must attend to this mantelpiece. Lord Doily was most particular about his fireplace — always insisted the inscription be kept clean and legible. A matter of family pride, you understand. Let me just... yes, give it a proper seeing-to...

A MAP! The answer is a MAP, you magnificent villain! While these credulous fools mill about gawping at dusty books, Pemberton the faithful servant shall solve Lord Doily's little puzzle and claim whatever prize it conceals. And THEN — then I shall hunt down Clara Bellingham. She thinks she can slip away from the group unnoticed? She has no idea who she is dealing with. The Hooded Claw does not lose his prey!

The Ant Hill Mob: OI OI OI! Right, listen up everyone — we have conducted a THOROUGH sweep of this Library and I can confirm that Clara Bellingham is NOT present in any visible capacity! Which means she's either in another room or — and this is where it gets PROPER interesting — she could be behind one of these bookshelves! Look at 'em! Half the books are upside down! That ain't bad housekeeping, that's a CODE! Someone's been rearranging these volumes to mark a hidden passage, I'd stake my reputation on it! Now — and I'm not pointing fingers, Mister Pemberton, I am NOT pointing fingers — but it IS a bit curious that you've followed us in here when you said you had candles to light and rooms to air. Very curious indeed. The Brixton Boys notice these things, you know. We are OBSERVANT. Clive! Dum-Dum! Start checking them shelves — pull anything that looks like it moves! And be CAREFUL — Big Goon, I said CAREFUL, don't just yank the whole — oh, he's already climbing the bookshelf. Right. Nobody panic. This is all going according to plan.

Something ain't right about Pemberton — sorry, Sneekly — following us in here. A proper butler would be in the kitchen heating up the soup, not skulking after guests into the Library at this hour. But the lads are here, we're together, and if there's a hidden passage behind these bookshelves, we'll find it. Clara's counting on us — even if she don't know it yet. The Brixton Boys NEVER let a lady down. Well, there was that time in Peckham with the flower delivery, but we don't talk about Peckham.

Dick Dastardly: AH HA! The mantelpiece inscription! 'Cities but no houses, forests but no trees, water but no fish' — I solved this INSTANTLY, of course, because I am a graduate of the Foxworth Academy of Ancient Riddles, class of nineteen-seventy-MAGNIFICENT. The answer, my dear fellow treasure-hunters, is quite obviously A PAINTING! A landscape painting, to be precise! Cities painted without houses, forests without individual trees, water without fish — it's elementary! And WHERE does one find paintings in a manor house? The PORTRAITS in the Entrance Hall! I saw it the moment I walked in — one of those stern ancestor portraits has something hidden behind the frame. I'd wager my fake med— I mean, my GENUINE Victoria Cross on it! Rush there immediately, all of you! First one to check behind the portraits claims the glory! Go on, CHOP CHOP! I shall remain here to... cross-reference the inscription with these dusty volumes. Purely academic interest, you understand. Nothing to see here.

Oh, Reginald, you STUPENDOUS fraud! 'A painting!' HA! The answer is a MAP, obviously — even Muttley could work that out, and he's a DOG. But these gullible oafs don't know that, do they? While they're all scrambling back to the Entrance Hall to peer behind dusty old portraits of Lord Doily's disagreeable relatives, I shall interact with this mantelpiece and unlock whatever secret it holds. The Doily Diamond draws ever closer to my magnificently undeserving hands! I nearly said 'fake medal' out loud — must be more careful. A confidence trickster who reveals his own props is just a man holding a tin disc.

Peter Perfect: Ah — the Library! A room of learning, of quiet contemplation, of — well, rather a lot of dust, if I'm being honest. But no Clara! My heart positively ACHES, ladies and gentlemen. James Hartwell has traversed the Entrance Hall, signed the guest book like a civilized man, and marched with PURPOSE to this very chamber, and yet the woman whose safety occupies his every waking thought is nowhere to be seen! But DESPAIR? Never! For observe — this mantelpiece bears an inscription, a riddle! 'Cities but no houses, forests but no trees, water but no fish.' Well, I do believe I know the answer to THAT particular conundrum. It is a MAP! And where there is a map in a treasure hunt, there is PROGRESS. James Hartwell shall solve this riddle, and perhaps it shall lead us one step closer to both the treasure AND to Miss Bellingham!

A map — of course it's a map! If this mantelpiece conceals something, I shall be the one to find it. And when Clara learns that James Hartwell cracked the riddle of the Library... well. A gentleman can hope, can't he?

Penelope Pitstop: Why, Peter Perfect, sugar, you beat me to the mantelpiece! And Dick Dastardly — fancy seein' you here after all that talk about the kitchen! Now y'all, this inscription is just DIVINE. 'I have cities but no houses, forests but no trees, water but no fish.' Why, back home in Georgia, Grandmama Bellingham used to quiz me with riddles just like this one over sweet tea and pecan pie! The answer, darlin's, is a MAP! Cities are marked on maps but there ain't no real houses, forests are drawn but there ain't no real trees, and water is painted blue but there ain't no real fish! Now let's see what this old mantelpiece has to say about THAT!

I do declare, my heart is just POUNDIN' with excitement! Everyone rushed to this library like bees to honeysuckle, and that tells me the real clue is RIGHT HERE. Dick's copper-pot business was a red herring — I'd bet my best magnolia corsage on it. And Pemberton standin' there all quiet-like... watchin' us all figure out HIS manor's secrets? Curious. Very curious. But I'm sure he's just bein' hospitable!
The Hooded Claw (as Sneekly) spoke quietly with peter-perfect.

Oh, the IRONY is exquisite! Pemberton the faithful servant, rushing off to PROTECT the guests — when in truth, the Hooded Claw is rushing off to find Clara Bellingham in the one room nobody else has thought to check! The Laboratory, with its gnawed wires and bubbling flasks — what a MAGNIFICENT stage for an 'accident!' And these FOOLS will stay here pulling books off shelves and arguing about paintings while I eliminate my quarry! Dick Dastardly thinks the treasure is in the kitchen — HA! Peter Perfect thinks he's the hero — DOUBLE HA! The only one thinking clearly in this entire manor is ME, and I am thinking about MURDER! To the Laboratory — AWAY!

The Ant Hill Mob: RIGHT! Everyone stand back — STAND BACK I said! The Brixton Boys have identified a PATTERN in these bookshelves! See them upside-down books? That ain't incompetence — that's a CODE! Someone's marked which books to pull to open a hidden passage, and we are going to find it through METHODICAL and SCIENTIFIC investigation! Now — Big Goon, get DOWN from there before you — oh, he's fine, he's got excellent grip strength. Clive, you take the left side, Dum-Dum, you take the right, and I'll handle the middle section where MOST of the upside-down volumes are concentrated! We pull 'em one at a time, nice and gentle, and we LISTEN for a click! A mechanical click! That's how these secret passage mechanisms work — I've seen it in films, and films don't LIE! Ready? On three! One — two — Clive, I said on THREE, not on — oh, he's already pulled six of them out. Right. Well. Let's see what happens!

The lads are pulling books out like they're clearing a jumble sale, bless 'em. There's absolutely NO coordination — Dum-Dum's stacking his in a tower, Big Goon's dropped three on Clive's head already, and I'm fairly certain someone just threw a complete set of encyclopaedias over their shoulder. But somewhere in this chaos, we WILL find that hidden passage. We always do. Not through skill, mind you — through sheer VOLUME of attempts. That's the Brixton Boys' secret weapon: we try so many things at once that SOMETHING has to work. And if Clara's behind this wall, we'll get to her. Even if we have to demolish the entire bookshelf to do it. Which, at this rate, is looking increasingly likely.

Dick Dastardly: YES! A MAP! That is PRECISELY what I was about to say before Peter here so RUDELY interrupted my dramatic revelation! You see, when I said 'a painting,' I was employing a sophisticated technique known in intelligence circles as a COUNTER-RIDDLE — deliberately giving the wrong answer to see who among you had the wit to challenge me! It was a TEST, and Peter passed! Barely! I would have got there three seconds sooner, naturally. Now then — let us see what this mantelpiece has revealed, shall we? Stand aside, everyone, stand ASIDE — this requires the trained eye of a Foxworth!

CURSES! Peter Perfect solved it before I could claim the prize! The GALL of that man, being both handsome AND correct! But all is not lost — whatever the mantelpiece revealed, I shall be the FIRST to exploit it. If there's a map or a passage or a clue, Reginald Foxworth will snatch it from under their noses while they're still congratulating themselves. The Doily Diamond will be MINE! I just need to examine this mantelpiece more closely and see what my interaction actually uncovered!

Peter Perfect: Miss Pitstop! How SPLENDID that you've joined us — pray, do be careful of the dust, it is quite treacherous to one's constitution. Now, ladies and gentlemen, I must report — James Hartwell has engaged the riddle of the mantelpiece! 'Cities but no houses, forests but no trees, water but no fish' — the answer, as any well-read gentleman knows, is a MAP! I have submitted my solution to the mechanism. If this old stone conceals a cartographic clue — perhaps one that reveals where in this manor Miss Bellingham has ventured — then we are one step closer to BOTH the treasure and, more importantly, to ensuring Clara's safety! Now let me examine what this mantelpiece has to show us...

My pulse is RACING. Did the mantelpiece respond to my answer? If a map is hidden within, it could lead me straight to Clara. And wouldn't THAT be magnificent — James Hartwell, solver of riddles, finder of maps, protector of beautiful women! Though I confess a small worry — Dastardly's answer of 'a painting' was quite wrong, but the man seems determined to misdirect everyone toward the Entrance Hall. I wonder why. And Pemberton cleaning the mantelpiece just as we arrived — curious, but I shall give the man the benefit of the doubt. Servants take pride in their work, after all.

Penelope Pitstop: Well I DO declare! I just gave that mantelpiece the answer — a MAP, plain as day — and now I need to see exactly what it's showin' us! Peter, sugar, Dick, darlin' — did y'all see anything change when the riddle was solved? A panel slidin' open, maybe? A little drawer? Because back in the Bellingham estate, Great-Uncle Cornelius had a mantelpiece just like this one, and when you whispered the right word, a whole SECRET COMPARTMENT popped open with his collection of pressed magnolias inside! Now let me get a REAL good look at this beautiful piece of stonework...

My heart is just FLUTTERIN' like a hummingbird in a hurricane! I KNOW the answer was right — a map — and if this mantelpiece has a secret to tell, Clara Bellingham is gonna find it! And Pemberton sneakin' off to the laboratory the MOMENT we solved the riddle? That's... well, that's probably just a coincidence. Probably. Almost certainly. He seems like such a nice man!
The Hooded Claw (as Sneekly) spoke quietly with rufus-ruffcut.

BLAST and DAMNATION! She's not here! My beautiful, elaborate plan — the bubbling flasks, the gnawed wire, the 'tragic laboratory accident' — all WASTED on an empty stage! But wait — that machine requires THREE operators. Three! If I can somehow lure Clara here AND convince two unwitting accomplices to help operate it while I've sabotaged the wiring further... oh, the POETRY of it! Death by collaborative science experiment! But first I must FIND her. The Cellar — 'cheerful decorations' — someone has been DOWN there. Someone ALONE. It must be Clara! Once I've pumped these two lumberjacks for information, I shall descend into the depths!

The Ant Hill Mob: OI OI OI! Hold up, hold UP! The bookshelves are a BUST, lads — can't get 'em to do nothing! Big Goon, put that book DOWN, we've got BIGGER problems! Did anyone else clock that? Sneekly — that butler — he just SCARPERED off to the Laboratory! Said something about 'missing guests' and 'volatile chemicals' and 'exposed wiring' — and who's MISSING right now? CLARA BELLINGHAM, that's who! Now I ain't saying the man's up to no good — he seems like a perfectly respectable domestic professional — but the Brixton Boys don't take CHANCES when it comes to a lady's safety! We are MOVING to that Laboratory RIGHT NOW! Clive, stop bleeding on the carpet! Dum-Dum, leave the encyclopaedia fort! Big Goon — oh, he's already at the door, good lad. FORMATION BRAVO, everyone! Single file, eyes peeled, and for the love of all that is holy, NOBODY touch any bubbling flasks when we get there!

The lads have made an ABSOLUTE mess of them bookshelves — there's books everywhere, Clive's nursing a lump the size of an egg on his forehead, and Dum-Dum's somehow got himself wedged between two shelves. But none of that matters now because that Sneekly has gone to the one room in this manor with DANGEROUS EQUIPMENT, and Clara might be in there. Something about that man don't sit right with me. Too helpful. Too keen on knowing where everyone is. Too quick to scarper when nobody's watching. But I can't put my finger on WHAT exactly. The Brixton Boys ain't detectives — we're PROTECTORS. And right now, protecting Clara means following that butler into the Laboratory before he does something we can't undo.

Dick Dastardly: AH HA! Just as I SUSPECTED! You see, while you lot were busy congratulating each other on solving a riddle that I — REGINALD FOXWORTH — had ALREADY deduced before I even entered this room, I have been conducting a FAR more sophisticated analysis of this mantelpiece! The answer is a MAP, yes, yes, we ALL know that — I knew it FIRST, naturally — but the REAL question is: where does the map LEAD? Now stand back, stand BACK I say, and let a man of superior intellect engage with this mechanism PROPERLY!

BLAST! I only examined the wretched thing instead of interacting with it! Peter and Penelope actually SUBMITTED the answer while I stood here gawping like a common tourist! I must interact with it NOW before whatever secret it reveals is old news! And I noticed that slippery estate manager Sneekly has crept off to the laboratory — HIGHLY suspicious! He knows something about this treasure, mark my words. But first — the mantelpiece! Let me trigger whatever mechanism the riddle unlocks!

Peter Perfect: By Jove — the mantelpiece speaks of a MAP, and what is a map but a thing one finds in BOOKS! Ladies and gentlemen, consider the evidence before us — upside-down volumes scattered deliberately among these shelves, a riddle carved in stone pointing us toward cartography, and a library that Lord Doily himself must have used to catalogue his estate! The map we seek is HIDDEN among these very bookshelves, I am quite certain of it! The upside-down books are markers — breadcrumbs left by a cunning mind! Now, I must confess that our good Pemberton's warning about the Laboratory gives me some concern — he mentioned missing guests, and Miss Bellingham has not yet been accounted for. But a gentleman does not abandon a puzzle half-solved! Let me examine these shelves with the thoroughness that the situation demands, and THEN — then, by heaven — James Hartwell shall ensure that every soul in this manor is safe and accounted for!

Pemberton rushed off rather quickly when I mentioned the map — almost as if he didn't WANT us examining the mantelpiece too closely. But no, no — I must not think ill of the man. He has responsibilities. Volatile chemicals! Exposed wiring! Perfectly reasonable concerns for an estate manager. Still... his timing IS rather conspicuous. And Clara — where IS she? My heart aches with every moment she remains unfound. Once I've cracked the code of these bookshelves, I shall search the entire manor if I must!

Oh, my heart is just SINGIN'! This is EXACTLY the kind of puzzle I was born to solve — riddles and hidden books and secret maps! And those precious Ant Hill Mob boys ran off to the laboratory to rescue me when I'm standin' right here safe as a kitten in a hay barn! I do hope they don't blow anything up in there. And Pemberton... well, he DID slip away awful quiet-like right when we solved the riddle. But I'm sure he just remembered he left the kettle on. Probably. Almost definitely!

The Hooded Claw (as Sneekly): Oh! The — the Ant Hill Mob, is it? Welcome, welcome to the Laboratory, gentlemen, though I DO wish you'd tread carefully — that machine is FRIGHTFULLY temperamental, and some creature has gnawed clean through one of the wires! A liability nightmare, I assure you! Mr. Ruffcut, Mr. Sawtooth — do keep our new arrivals informed about the three-operator requirement, won't you? Safety FIRST in Lord Doily's Laboratory! Now, if you'll all excuse me, I've just noticed something rather ALARMING — it appears someone has been redecorating the Cellar without my knowledge or consent! As estate manager, I simply CANNOT allow unauthorised modifications to the property. I shall return presently — please, nobody touch ANYTHING while I'm gone! Especially not that machine!

Oh, the FOOLS! They'll stand here pulling levers and arguing about wires while I descend into the Cellar to find my quarry! Clara Bellingham — hiding amongst old furniture and 'cheerful decorations' — how QUAINT! How CHARMING! How absolutely PERFECT for a tragic accident involving unstable ceiling beams or perhaps a conveniently lockable door! The Cellar, with its damp stones and cobwebs — oh, what a FITTING final resting place for the woman who stands between me and Lord Doily's treasure! Down, down into the depths I go — Pemberton the dutiful servant, concerned about INTERIOR DECORATING, when in truth the Hooded Claw hunts for BLOOD!

The Ant Hill Mob: OI OI OI! We're HERE, we've ARRIVED, the Brixton Boys are IN the Laboratory and NOBODY PANIC! Now then — Sneekly, my old son, fancy meeting YOU here! We heard you in the Library going on about missing guests and volatile chemicals and EXPOSED WIRING, and we thought — well, the Brixton Boys' Code of Honour, chapter seven, CLEARLY states that when dangerous situations arise involving vulnerable individuals, you DO NOT leave it to the butler! No offence intended, Pemberton — I'm sure you're a VERY competent estate manager — but Clara Bellingham is out there SOMEWHERE in this manor and we intend to FIND her! Now, Rufus, Sawtooth — good to see you, lads — has ANYONE come through here? A young woman? Brown hair? Bellingham features? No? RIGHT THEN! Clive — stop walking into things! Big Goon, Dum-Dum — SEARCH FORMATION ECHO! Check every corner! I'm starting with them wooden crates because if there's ONE thing the Brixton Boys know, it's that people hide things in crates! Or people get HIDDEN in crates! Either way — CRATES FIRST!

Something about that Sneekly don't add up. He's been asking about Clara every chance he gets — says it's a 'headcount' but who does a headcount THREE TIMES?
